title: Individual Article 19a threshold scope
plainEnglish: An undertaking falls within Article 19a where it exceeds EUR 450 million net turnover and an average of 1,000 employees during the financial year. Both thresholds are cumulative. Article 1(4) removes the European Financial Stability Facility and the financial products listed in points (b) and (f) of Article 2(12) of Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 from Article 19a; an undertaking whose exclusion status is unknown stays unresolved rather than being read as in scope.
caution: Threshold-crossing ranges are indeterminate — ask for the exact value. This is scope, not the final reporting duty (see CSRD-S-014); national transposition may vary timing and options.

title: Consolidated Article 29a threshold scope
plainEnglish: A parent undertaking falls within Article 29a where its group exceeds EUR 450 million net turnover and an average of 1,000 employees on a consolidated basis. This is the consolidated size test only; it does not decide whether or when the group must report. CSRD-S-014 composes the threshold and exemption results into the reporting duty, and the financial-year questions rest with CSRD-S-003, CSRD-S-004 (Article 5(2) of Directive (EU) 2022/2464) and the national overlay (CSRD-S-013). Article 1(4) removes the European Financial Stability Facility and the financial products listed in points (b) and (f) of Article 2(12) of Regulation (EU) 2019/2088 from Article 29a; an undertaking whose exclusion status is unknown stays unresolved rather than being read as in scope.
caution: Use the legal consolidation perimeter, not internal business units.

title: First-wave (FY2024) reporting history
plainEnglish: Prior FY2024 CSRD reporters are a distinct population; their FY2025–26 position depends on the amended thresholds and the governing Member State's transitional implementation.
caution: Never tell a former reporter to stop based only on an EU-level threshold screen (see CSRD-S-004 and CSRD-S-013).

title: FY2025–26 national transition exemption
plainEnglish: Member States may relieve undertakings that fall below either amended threshold for financial years beginning between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2026, where the national transition option is exercised.
caution: Requires the governing country pack — this is a national option, not a universal automatic exemption.

title: Subsidiary exemption via qualifying EU-parent consolidated report
plainEnglish: A subsidiary may be exempt from individual sustainability reporting where it is included in a qualifying EU parent consolidated sustainability report and the publication, identification and related conditions are met. Where the subsidiary is itself a parent undertaking, its own subsidiary undertakings must be included in the same report (Article 19a(9): 'such undertaking and its subsidiary undertakings'); inclusion of the subsidiary alone does not establish the exemption. The exemption turns on where the parent that draws up the report is established, which may differ from the group's ultimate parent, and it is conditional on the exempted undertaking's own management report carrying the disclosures of Article 19a(9), second subparagraph, point (a) — the reporting parent's name and registered office, the weblinks to its report and assurance opinion, and the statement of exemption — unless the undertaking is exempted from preparing a management report under Article 37 and publishes the consolidated management report as Article 37 requires, which is stated and never assumed.
caution: Scope and exemption are separate determinations: 'threshold in scope but exempt' must never be summarised as 'CSRD does not apply'. Exemption evidence must remain current every year (O-011).

title: Subsidiary exemption via qualifying non-EU parent report
plainEnglish: A subsidiary of a non-EU parent may be exempt where it is included in a qualifying parent report prepared under ESRS or standards deemed equivalent, with assurance, required EU Taxonomy information and publication conditions met. Where the subsidiary is itself a parent undertaking, its own subsidiary undertakings must be included in the same report (Article 19a(9): 'such undertaking and its subsidiary undertakings'); inclusion of the subsidiary alone does not establish the exemption. The exemption turns on where the parent that draws up the report is established, which may differ from the group's ultimate parent, and it is conditional on the exempted undertaking's own management report carrying the disclosures of Article 19a(9), second subparagraph, point (a) — the reporting parent's name and registered office, the weblinks to its report and assurance opinion, and the statement of exemption — unless the undertaking is exempted from preparing a management report under Article 37 and publishes the consolidated management report as Article 37 requires, which is stated and never assumed.
caution: 'EQUIVALENT' requires a formal equivalence basis — treat as legal judgment with a signed DecisionRecord until an equivalence decision exists.

title: Article 40a third-country group gate
plainEnglish: A non-EU ultimate parent enters the Article 40a route where it generated more than EUR 450 million net turnover in the EU in each of the last two consecutive financial years. The two years are tested separately, never averaged. The route applies for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2028.

title: Article 40a subsidiary gateway
plainEnglish: The Article 40a route applies through an EU subsidiary where the group gate is met and that subsidiary exceeded EUR 200 million net turnover in the preceding financial year.
caution: The subsidiary is a publication gateway, not necessarily the reporting parent. Art. 40a reporting runs for financial years beginning on or after 1 January 2028 (R-012).

title: Article 40a branch gateway
plainEnglish: A branch is the gateway where the group gate is met, no qualifying EU subsidiary exists, and the branch exceeded EUR 200 million net turnover in the preceding financial year.
caution: Evaluate the branch gateway only after the subsidiary gateway.

title: Protected value-chain undertaking
plainEnglish: A value-chain undertaking with no more than 1,000 average employees in the preceding financial year receives statutory protection from above-cap CSRD information requests made by a CSRD reporter for its CSRD reporting.
caution: This is NOT a direct CSRD reporting duty and the cap is purpose-limited: it does not restrict requests made for due diligence, lending or other purposes (R-016). Do not infer purpose from the requestor's identity.

title: Above-cap request with decline right
plainEnglish: Where a protected undertaking receives a CSRD-purpose request containing items beyond the voluntary-standard cap, it may decline the above-cap items; the requestor must identify the excess and communicate the right to decline.
caution: The cap protection does not extend to GHG emissions metrics — never advise declining emissions-data requests on cap grounds. The item catalogue versions against the voluntary-standard delegated act, which is adopted but not yet in force; mappings stay provisional until then.

title: Applicable ESRS version
plainEnglish: The reporting undertaking must use the legally applicable ESRS version for its financial year. The 2023 ESRS (with the 2025 quick-fix) remain the baseline until the revised 2026 ESRS become legally effective.

cases.label: Revised act not yet in force — 2023 ESRS (incl. quick-fix) apply regardless of FY
Revised ESRS mandatory for FY beginning on or after 1 Jan 2027
FY2026 early adoption once the revised act is in force

caution: The revised ESRS were adopted 3 Jul 2026 but were NOT in force at the pack snapshot; they must not alter current obligations until legal effectiveness (Change Watch CW-001).

title: National-law completeness gate
plainEnglish: A final customer answer must identify the governing Member State and rest on its current transposition status, filing calendar, publication rules and exercised options. Until the country rules are encoded and ratified, no EU-level screen is a final legal conclusion.
caution: CSRD is directive-based law. A negative EU-level threshold result with this gate unresolved must read 'EU-level threshold not met; national-law status requires review' — never 'CSRD does not apply'.

title: Reporting duty (post-exemption)
plainEnglish: An active sustainability-reporting duty exists where either route applies: the individual route (CSRD-S-020: the Article 19a measures apply to the undertaking for the financial year and no individual exemption removes them) or the consolidated route (CSRD-S-021: the Article 29a measures apply to the parent for the financial year and no consolidated exemption removes them). Required information belongs in a clearly identifiable section of the (consolidated) management report.
caution: A standalone promotional sustainability report is not automatically sufficient. First reporting year is decided per route by CSRD-S-017 and CSRD-S-018 (Article 5(2) of Directive (EU) 2022/2464); the filing calendar and the exercised national options resolve through the national overlay (CSRD-S-013), and no answer here is a final legal conclusion until the country pack is ratified.

title: Limited assurance over sustainability reporting
plainEnglish: Statutory sustainability information is subject to limited assurance under the amended audit framework wherever the reporting duty is active.
caution: Provider eligibility and appointment rules require the national overlay. Limited assurance remains the mandatory level; the assurance standard is due by 1 July 2027.

title: First-three-years value-chain transition relief
plainEnglish: During the first three reporting years, the undertaking may explain unavailable value-chain information and the efforts and plans to obtain it.
caution: Track the first reporting year as a sourced fact.

title: Individual first application (Article 5(2) of Directive (EU) 2022/2464)
plainEnglish: The Article 19a measures apply to an undertaking for the assessed financial year under one of two routes: for financial years starting between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2026, where it is a large undertaking (Article 3(4)) that is a public-interest entity (Article 2(1)) with more than 500 average employees; or for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027, where it meets the amended Article 19a(1) size test (CSRD-S-001). An undertaking excluded by Article 1(4) is outside both routes in every year: the first-wave route tests the exclusion itself, and the 2027 route inherits it from the size test. Whether the measures apply is a different question from whether the size test passes and from whether an exemption removes the duty (CSRD-S-020).
caution: The Directive's own calendar. Which measures apply in a given year is decided by the governing Member State's transposition (CSRD-S-013); the FY2025–26 national derogation on the individual basis is CSRD-S-004. Issuers reach this route because admission to a regulated market makes them public-interest entities; the Transparency Directive measures of Article 5(2), third subparagraph, are not encoded. Article 1(3) as amended conditions the extension to credit institutions and insurance undertakings regardless of legal form on the amended thresholds; whether that narrows the first-wave route for such undertakings below those thresholds is an open source question recorded in the design.

title: Consolidated first application (Article 5(2) of Directive (EU) 2022/2464)
plainEnglish: The Article 29a measures apply to a parent undertaking for the assessed financial year under one of two routes: for financial years starting between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2026, where it is a public-interest entity (Article 2(1)) that is the parent of a large group (Article 3(7)) with more than 500 average employees on a consolidated basis; or for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2027, where its group meets the amended Article 29a(1) size test (CSRD-S-002). A parent excluded by Article 1(4) is outside both routes in every year: the first-wave route tests the exclusion itself, and the 2027 route inherits it from the size test. Whether the measures apply is a different question from whether the size test passes and from whether an exemption removes the duty (CSRD-S-021).
caution: The Directive's own calendar. Which measures apply in a given year is decided by the governing Member State's transposition (CSRD-S-013); the FY2025–26 national derogation on the consolidated basis is CSRD-S-022. Issuers reach this route because admission to a regulated market makes them public-interest entities; the Transparency Directive measures of Article 5(2), third subparagraph, are not encoded. Article 1(3) as amended conditions the extension to credit institutions and insurance undertakings regardless of legal form on the amended thresholds; whether that narrows the first-wave route for such undertakings below those thresholds is an open source question recorded in the design.

title: Consolidated exemption via a higher parent's qualifying report
plainEnglish: A parent undertaking that is itself a subsidiary is exempted from consolidated sustainability reporting where it and its subsidiary undertakings are included in another undertaking's consolidated management report drawn up under Articles 29 and 29a, or in a third-country parent's consolidated sustainability reporting carried out under ESRS or equivalent standards with an assurance opinion and the EU Taxonomy information, its own management report carries the Article 29a(8) disclosures (or it is exempted from preparing a management report under Article 37 and publishes the consolidated management report as Article 37 requires, which is stated and never assumed), and the publication conditions are met. The exemption also applies to public-interest entities (Article 29a(9)). Inclusion of the parent alone, without its subsidiaries, does not establish it. The route — the Articles 29/29a sentence or the third-country sentence — follows where the parent that draws up the report is established, which may differ from the group's ultimate parent.
caution: Scope and exemption are separate determinations: 'threshold in scope but exempt' must never be summarised as 'CSRD does not apply'. 'EQUIVALENT' requires a formal equivalence basis — treat as legal judgment with a signed DecisionRecord until an equivalence decision exists (as CSRD-S-006). Credit institutions permanently affiliated to a central body, insurance undertakings under group supervision and the Article 48i transitional reporting are analyst and country-pack matters; the reporting parent's country is stated (parent.reporting_parent_country), never inferred from the ultimate parent's. Exemption evidence must remain current every year (O-011).

title: Individual reporting duty (Article 19a)
plainEnglish: The undertaking has an individual sustainability-reporting duty where the Article 19a measures apply to it for the assessed financial year (CSRD-S-017) and no individual exemption — the FY2025–26 national derogation (CSRD-S-004) or a subsidiary exemption (CSRD-S-005, CSRD-S-006) — removes them. The size test enters only through the first-application rule's 2027 route, so a first-wave public-interest entity below the amended thresholds keeps its FY2024–26 duty.
caution: An EU-level screen: the governing Member State's transposition, filing calendar and exercised options resolve through CSRD-S-013, and no answer here is a final legal conclusion until the country pack is ratified.

title: Consolidated reporting duty (Article 29a)
plainEnglish: The parent undertaking has a consolidated sustainability-reporting duty where the Article 29a measures apply to it for the assessed financial year (CSRD-S-018) and no consolidated exemption — the FY2025–26 national derogation on a consolidated basis (CSRD-S-022), the Article 29a(8) exemption (CSRD-S-019) or the Article 29a(7a) financial-holding option (CSRD-S-023) — removes them. An individual exemption of the parent never removes this duty.
caution: An EU-level screen: the governing Member State's transposition, filing calendar and exercised options resolve through CSRD-S-013, and no answer here is a final legal conclusion until the country pack is ratified. Use the legal consolidation perimeter, not internal business units.

title: FY2025–26 national transition exemption, consolidated basis
plainEnglish: Member States may relieve a parent undertaking whose group, on a consolidated basis, falls below either amended threshold for financial years beginning between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2026, where the national transition option is exercised. The consolidated twin of CSRD-S-004: Article 5(2), fifth subparagraph, applies 'on a consolidated basis where applicable', so the consolidated figures govern the consolidated duty and the individual figures the individual duty.
caution: Requires the governing country pack — this is a national option, not a universal automatic exemption.

title: Financial-holding option under Article 29a(7a) (deferred encoding)
plainEnglish: A parent undertaking that is a financial holding undertaking (Article 2(15)) whose subsidiary undertakings' business models and operations are independent of one another may choose not to include the consolidated sustainability information in its consolidated management report. Encoded as a bracket on the consolidated duty: a stated exercise of the option over independent subsidiaries relieves the parent at EU level; an unknown holding status, independence or exercise stays unresolved and is never read as 'not exercised'; a parent that is not a financial holding undertaking is untouched.
caution: Deferred encoding: the Member State's implementation of the option, the content an opted-out parent still reports and any national conditions are not encoded and resolve through CSRD-S-013 and analyst review; a relief recorded here is an EU-level screen, not a final legal conclusion.
